my visit to Riverside Surgery - Pier Road Branch on (19/11/24). The encounter left me feeling disrespected, humiliated, and deeply disheartened as a patient with a disability.
Upon arriving for my blood test appointment, my husband waited at the reception desk for at least 10 minutes to check me in, as I have reduced mobility and rely on support. Despite his visible presence, the receptionist appeared to ignore him completely, typing on her computer and pretending not to notice.
Frustrated by the lack of acknowledgement and aware of my limited mobility, I attempted to use the self-check-in kiosk. Unfortunately, the system did not recognize my appointment. With no other option, I approached the receptionist myself, using my walking stick. Astonishingly, she again acted as if I were invisible, further ignoring me.
It was only when another patient arrived and casually leaned on the reception desk that the receptionist finally paid attention. After addressing this other patient, I informed her that I had a blood test appointment. She responded by asking for my blood test form, which I explained I had been told was not required when the appointment was booked.
Instead of resolving the matter professionally, the receptionist insisted I needed the form, stating I could not have my blood specimen taken without it. She knew all along that she needed to print the form for me and booked me in. —a task that should have been completed without such unnecessary delays or stress. The entire interaction felt like a deliberate run-around, wasting my time and energy.
The way I was treated—ignored, dismissed, and forced to endure repeated explanations—was deeply dehumanising. I felt humiliated, as though my disability and needs were being overlooked or trivialised.
